# Overview {.unnumbered}

Thank you for visiting my portfolio of selected Data Science projects. To avoid repetition, principles and components common to several or all of my repositories (repos) are detailed below. Projects are covered in individual detail in their respective chapters.

# Data Security
Components in my projects relating to principles of Data Security exist to ensure sensitive, personal, or otherwise voluminous data does not get committed or pushed to the remote repo.

## .gitignore
I use .gitignores tailored to the tech stack of the project (R, Python, Quarto etc.). Where possible, exceptions are indicated as full filepaths rather than with regex expressions.

## githooks/
I use a pre-commit githook to prevent files likely to contain data (.csv, .xlsx, etc.) from being committed, if they are not caught by the .gitignore.

# Reproducibility
Components in my projects relating to reproducibility exist to best enable people to use and contribute to the work. Much of this is guided by the paradigm of Reproducible Analytical Pipelines (RAP).

## uv & renv
To ensure my work is reproducible across different machines and different global configurations, I use virtual environments to manage packages - renv for R, and uv for Python.

## LICENSE
My public repos include an MIT licence so that they can be used by others.

# CI/CD

## .github/
My projects with Github Pages deployments include a Github Action to build and deploy every time I merge a branch into main.
